editorial:
Imagine waking up in the middle of a giant city and suddenly the ground starts shaking like crazy. That is exactly how you start this ride. You get to follow several different people across Tokyo as they try to survive a massive earthquake. It feels like a high-stakes race against time because the city is falling apart around them. The vibe is very tense, and since it was made for TV, it has that old-school feel where the drama is dialed up to ten. You will find yourself rooting for the characters to find their families while everything collapses.

What really works here is how the movie shows the panic of a crowd. The acting is solid for a TV movie, and the pacing keeps you on your toes without feeling too slow. While the special effects look a bit dated now, they still give you a good sense of the danger. If you love disaster flicks, you should definitely check this out. Since it is an older gem, you might want to look for a remastered 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection for the best quality, or see if you can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night.
endingExplained: As the shaking finally stops, the movie shows the total wreckage of Tokyo. Most of the main characters manage to reunite with their loved ones, but the city is left in ruins. The final scenes focus on the long road to recovery and the sadness of those who lost everything. It ends on a hopeful note, showing people helping each other rebuild their lives from the rubble of the disaster.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old school disaster movies and survival stories.
